message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t give you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
For the most up‑to‑date information you can check:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the current AQI, pollutant breakdown, and forecast. |
| **AQICN** | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and see the latest AQI, historical trends, and health recommendations. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or smartphone weather widgets) | Many include an AQI indicator for major cities. |
| **Local news sites** | They often report on smog alerts or air‑quality advisories. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They pull from the same public data sources.
